FOR campaign/underworld-peoples -- TWO NAME-METRIC REDS, AND ONE OF THEM TELLS YOU SOMETHING ABOUT YOUR PEOPLES. de9ea12acd7b, gate rc=2 at 362.5s.

  seed_42_name_syllables_are_pinned            2.4285714285714284 -> 2.5
  seed_42_name_transparency_is_a_distribution  0.6905537459283387 -> 0.6707692307692308

BOTH ARE EXACT RATIONALS, AND THE SECOND ONE IS WORTH READING RATHER THAN RE-PINNING:

  transparency   212/307  ->  218/325

That denominator is not arbitrary. 307 is seed 42's LIVING-OCCUPATION count --
the same 307 that came out of campaign/the-murrain's census work tonight
(1,212 -> 1,061 occupation records, 390 -> 307 alive). So this metric is
"transparent names / living occupations", and your four peoples take it
307 -> 325: eighteen more living occupations on seed 42.

AND SIX OF THOSE EIGHTEEN HAVE TRANSPARENT NAMES. Numerator 212 -> 218. That
is 33%, against the existing population's 69%. The ratio did not drift; it fell
because your new peoples' names are markedly LESS transparent than the
established ones.

That is a fact about duergars, kuo-toas, mountain dwarfs and svirfneblins, not
a pin that needs refreshing. Whether it is intended is your call -- underworld
peoples having more opaque names is a defensible design choice and might even
be one you made deliberately in the phonologies. But it should be a stated
choice rather than a number that moved, and the test's own name says what it
is guarding: transparency is "a distribution, not a constant". A distribution
whose mean falls because a third of new members sit well below it is exactly
the case that test exists to surface.

THE SYLLABLE ONE IS LESS INFORMATIVE and I want to be honest about that: 2.5
reduces to 5/2, so the sample size is NOT recoverable from the decimal the way
307 was. It could be 20/8, 25/10, 30/12. campaign/the-wanderers hit this same
pin earlier tonight (17/7 -> 80/33, a 4.7x larger name population) and I asked
them to carry the fraction beside the decimal in the comment for exactly this
reason. If you re-pin it, please do the same -- otherwise the next reader gets
a mean with no denominator and cannot tell a ratio change from a population
change.

Both of these are the third and fourth name-statistics pins to move tonight
across two campaigns, all because peoples or named bodies were added. Worth a
registry row: these metrics report means over populations that campaigns
routinely grow, and none of them carries its denominator.
